build_plan.exit_criteria: Sun body 189.213 by 183.186 by 6.2 mm with 24 blind lane pockets, an unbroken edge circle at radius 79.70 mm, 32 separate flames rooted on it with no adjacent roots touching, no closed loop anywhere, a width at half length of at least 45 per cent of the root width, tip caps between 2.00 and 2.60 mm, at least one flame in three leaning the minority way in runs of one to three, and no two flames closer than 0.80 mm; and 24 lane tiles ending on one exact arc at radius 79.55 mm with a constant 0.70 mm orange margin. Wall and overhang gates pass on all 25 parts.
30 identical 10.0 by 7.0 by 4.5 mm teardrop drops in 2 filament tones, a counter at the outermost station fully supported on its own tile, and the wall and overhang gates passing on all 30.

components.duty: Carries the 24 playable points in 4 banks of 6, each with capacity 15 counters, plus the exposed centre bar that holds every displaced drop until it recirculates.
components.form: One printed disc of radius 79.70 mm and 6.2 mm total height. Its top carries 24 blind lane pockets 1.6 mm deep on a 15 degree pitch, a rim ring dropped 0.4 mm to carry the tile lips, and a 24.0 mm centre bar standing 0.8 mm proud with 4 engraved V ticks on the 4 bank boundaries. Its edge circle is unbroken, and 32 separate curled flames stand off that circle, each rooted on its own arc of it and parted from its neighbours by a valley of bare circle as wide as a root. A flame is broad where it meets the circle - 8.05 mm of root arc on average - holds three quarters of that width at half its length, and narrows hard into a blunt rounded cap 2.00 to 2.60 mm across. Fourteen of the 32 curl against the ring and 18 with it, in runs of one to three, so the fringe flicks rather than spins. The tallest flame reaches radius 96.70 mm.
components.interfaces: 24 blind pockets receive the 24 lane tiles through a 0.15 mm clearance on each side and a 6.0 mm locating key recess per lane; the bar top at 6.2 mm receives displaced drops.
components.name: Sun board
components.placement: Flat on the table, underside down, both people reaching its face. It is the only part that is not loose.

components.duty: Marks playable point 1 in the light tone and gives that point its own seated landing surface.
components.form: One tapered sector strip 2.2 mm thick over its seat and 1.0 mm over its outer lip, spanning radius 26.5 mm to 79.55 mm, its outer edge one exact circular arc, with a 6.0 by 1.6 mm locating key under it. No notch, bay or scallop is cut into any end of it.
components.interfaces: Its key drops into the pocket recess; its lip laps the rim ring at 5.0 mm; its top carries counters at 5 radial stations.
components.name: Lane tile 1
components.placement: Seated in the lane pocket on the -75 degree axis, top at 6.0 mm, standing 0.6 mm proud of the deck.

concept.interaction: Two people each take the 15 drops of one filament tone and supply their own ordinary six-sided die cup; the pair shares two ordinary 1-6 dice of any standard make, which the set does not include. The Sun board is set between them. Each rolls both dice and moves drops the exact die distances along the lane tiles, counting the printed points in opposite directions. Landing on a point holding one enemy drop displaces it onto the centre bar, and that drop must re-enter from the opposite home bank before its owner moves anything else. The first person to drain all 15 wins.
concept.summary: Backgammon on a Sun. Two streams of condensed plasma travel 24 radial lanes, scatter lone drops onto the exposed flare at the centre, and rain back out of play. The rim is a crown of 32 separate licks of flame standing off the disc's own circular edge, each twice as broad at the root as the fins it replaces and flicking left or right the way fire does, never all one way.
concept.title: Rainward Sunflare

baseline.note: This Make is a correction of an unreleased set. The cloned CAD supplies the construction, the plan mathematics, the rule ledger, the counter outline, the audit method and every dimension this Wish does not change. Only the corona changes: its count, its taper and its handedness.

research.current_access: No network access was used in this Make. Every claim here is read from the sealed Wish, the sealed reference images, the local clone, or measured on the built geometry.

design_changes.reason: The Wish fixes the count. It is also the count at which a fat root and an open valley can both exist: the tallest flame rises 17.0 mm, so its root wants about 8 mm, and 8 mm of root plus a valley as wide as a root needs the 15.649 mm pitch that 360/32 of this circle gives. Measured root arc is 7.665 to 8.424 mm against 5.104 to 5.622 mm before.

design_changes.decision: the half width falls as 1 - t**1.50 instead of (1 - t)**1.50
design_changes.previous: the surplus over the cap decayed fastest at the root and flattest at the tip
design_changes.reason: The old curve shed 65 per cent of the surplus by mid length and then ran the outer third out at cap width, which is the near-parallel filament the Wish names. Reversing the profile leaves the root flat and arrives at the cap steeply. Width at half length is now 0.7313 of the root width at worst against a floor of 0.45, and the flank converges on the cap at about 30 degrees per side instead of 2. Exponents 1.0, 1.5 and 2.2 were drawn as unwrapped silhouettes and compared against the concept before 1.5 was kept.

The earlier brief's one-sided 'treat 2.10 mm as the floor, not the target' is withdrawn by this Wish; it drove the caps to 4.10 mm, which read as thumbs. Against an 8.05 mm mean root the new cap is 0.240 to 0.332 of the base. Every tip is still a blunt rounded cap on a flame at least 3.312 mm tall in Z, so the needle test still passes.

design_changes.decision: 14 of the 32 flames curl the opposite way, in runs of one to three
design_changes.previous: every flame turned the same way
design_changes.reason: Two independent naive reads of the last build called it a rosette, a medallion and a pinwheel disc and never reached for sun, flame or fire: 'The uniform one-way handedness reads as rotation, which actively competes with the fire reading.' The printability argument for one handedness is withdrawn and was wrong - the corona lies flat in the print plane and a flame's curvature is entirely in X and Y, while the 45-degree rule governs Z only. The mirror is exact, so the root, turn magnitude, taper, cap, ramp and print pose are untouched. Narrowest gap between any two flames is 7.275 mm against the 0.80 mm floor, so no pair needed flipping. The walk constant was then moved from frac(sqrt(19)/2) to frac(sqrt(117)/2) after an independent blind critic read the first build's rim as 'a consistent counterclockwise sweep ... like a pinwheel' despite the correct 14/18 split: a flame's visible rake scales with its length, so only the eight tall flames carry the handedness at a glance, and under the old constant those eight fell into same-sign pairs. Six of the eight tall neighbours now differ, with the generator, run caps, minority share and run-length bounds unchanged.

design_changes.decision: the corona ring starts half a valley past zero degrees
design_changes.previous: flame 0's root started exactly on the disc cylinder's own seam
design_changes.reason: Two vertices a femtometre apart had to be merged there and the kernel resolved that tie differently from run to run, so the exported STEP alternated between two byte orderings differing only in the last bit of six coordinates. Starting the ring half a valley later puts bare base circle over the seam; six consecutive generations now hash identically. It is a constant rotation, so no measured arc, rise, turn, cap or clearance changes.

design_changes.decision: the tile fan, counters, stations, stack, colours and rules are untouched
design_changes.reason: The Wish puts the orange band out of scope: widening it means pulling the tile ring inward, which would strand the outermost counter station at radius 74.0. RULES.md is carried byte for byte and its sha256 was re-confirmed on the copied file.

research.inventor_method: Mara Masque reskins widely popular public-domain board games with astronomy-first themes while preserving their exact rules. The 1911 Backgammon rules are carried byte for byte; only the surface is coronal rain.

reference_images.read: The concept: a plain circular disc of 24 radial lanes, teardrop counters in two tones, player-supplied cups and dice, and a rim of separate licks of flame with open background between them. The licks are broad at the base, hold their width low down, narrow into points, and hook in opposite directions from one neighbour to the next.

The previous round's own unwrapped comparison, one third of the ring at radius 0.86 to 1.22 of the disc. Its built strip is the fault being corrected: 48 thin, uniformly same-handed fins that lose their width immediately above the root and run out as near-parallel filaments.

rules_ledger.note: Carried into this revision byte for byte; not edited.
